newsitem.title: CHINA: China, Japan ink memorandum on new air routes.
newsitem.headline: China, Japan ink memorandum on new air routes.

text.p: China and Japan on Friday signed a memorandum allowing more airlines to provide services between the two countries, increasing the number of air routes and expanding aviation cooperation, the Xinhua news agency said.

The memorandum, signed after four days of talks in the northern Chinese city of Tianjin, would increase the number of cities in China and Japan that were open to the two countries' airlines to 26 from 14, the agency said.

The number of cities with originating flights would increase to 26 from 12 and the number of airlines permitted to fly from them would be raised to six from four, allowing a 50 percent increase in flights between China and Japan, it said.
The agreement would go into effect by the end of August after final government approval from both sides, it said but did not elaborate.
